structural_difference_from_2026: CONFIRMED: NBC 2016 does NOT use a per-occupancy height-OR-area lookup table like 2026's applicability_thresholds.json. Instead it uses a single FLAT LIST of independent trigger conditions (clause 1, 'SCOPE') - if a building matches ANY one of the conditions below, the whole of Part 4 applies to it. There is also no synthetic Low/Medium/High 'height tier' system anywhere in the 2016 source - the product-scope assumption that 2026 'replaced a synthetic height tier system' does not describe 2016's actual mechanism; 2016's mechanism was already a flat height/area/occupancy trigger list, just structured very differently from 2026's clean per-occupancy table (2026 converted this into one row per occupancy with a single height AND single area figure, whichever is exceeded first).
rule_logic_2016: Part 4 applies to a building if ANY of the following independently trigger it (clause 1, SCOPE): (1) it is a 'high rise building' (>= 15 m in height, ANY occupancy); OR (2) it is a 'special building' - hotel, educational, institutional, business, mercantile, industrial, storage, hazardous, or mixed-occupancy - with floor area more than 500 sqm on any one or more floors; OR (3) it is an educational building with height >= 9 m; OR (4) it is an institutional building with height >= 9 m; OR (5) it is ANY assembly (Group D) building, unconditionally (no height/area floor at all); OR (6) it has more than 300 sqm of incidental assembly occupancy on any floor; OR (7) it has two or more basements, or one basement of area more than 500 sqm. A NOTE adds that an owner/parties to an agreement may voluntarily choose to apply Part 4 to buildings outside this list.

comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.note: Loosely reconstructing 2016's triggers into 2026's per-occupancy height/area shape for comparison purposes ONLY - this is an approximation, not a literal 2016 table (2016 has no such table):
comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.residential_A: 2016 has NO explicit standalone applicability trigger for Residential other than the >=15m high-rise rule and the >500 sqm 'special building' rule (residential is not separately named in the 'special building' list, and is not one of the always-in-scope groups) - i.e., a low-rise, small-footprint residential building appears to fall OUTSIDE 2016 Part 4's mandatory scope entirely, whereas 2026 sets an explicit Residential trigger at 24 m / 750 sqm. Verify this reading against the full clause 1 text before relying on it - the 'hotel' special-building item may have been intended to cover A-5/A-6 specifically rather than all of Group A.
comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.educational_B: 2016: height >= 9 m OR area > 500 sqm ('special building'). 2026: height >= 9 m OR area > 500 sqm. IDENTICAL thresholds for Educational.
comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.institutional_C: 2016: height >= 9 m OR area > 500 sqm. 2026: height >= 15 m OR area > 500 sqm. Height threshold TIGHTENED (LOWERED, i.e. more buildings brought into scope) in 2016 relative to 2026 for Institutional, or conversely RELAXED in 2026 - either way this is a genuine numeric difference worth flagging: 2016 pulls a 9-15 m institutional building into mandatory Part 4 scope where 2026 would not.
comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.assembly_D: 2016: ALL assembly buildings, unconditionally, no height or area floor. 2026: height >= 9 m OR area > 750 sqm - i.e. 2026 introduces a floor below which a small assembly building is technically out of scope, where 2016 had none. This is a significant relaxation from 2016 to 2026 for very small assembly occupancies, if the 2026 README's applicability table is read literally.
comparison_to_2026_per_occupancy_table.business_E_mercantile_F_industrial_G_sto: 2016: area > 500 sqm on any floor triggers scope ('special building' list), with no separate height trigger named for these groups (though the >=15m high-rise rule still applies on top, occupancy-independent). 2026 gives each of these its own explicit height OR area pair (e.g. Business 15m/750sqm, Mercantile 15m/1000sqm, Storage 9m/500sqm, Hazardous 9m/500sqm) - materially more granular than 2016's one-size-fits-all 500 sqm figure for this whole group of occupancies.

basement_trigger.rule: Two or more basements of any size, OR a single basement with area more than 500 sqm, brings a building into Part 4's scope regardless of occupancy or height.
basement_trigger.comparison_to_2026: No equivalent standalone basement-count/area applicability trigger was found in the 2026 applicability_thresholds.json reviewed for this task - flag for follow-up: either 2026 folded this into Table 7's per-occupancy basement notes instead of the top-level scope clause, or it was not captured in the 2026 digitization pass.

high_rise_definition.definition: A building 15 m or above in height, irrespective of its occupancy.
high_rise_definition.comparison_to_2026: 2026's high-rise flag threshold is 24 m (clause 2.39: is_high_rise = height_m >= 24). The 2016 threshold of 15 m is SUBSTANTIALLY LOWER - a building between 15 m and 24 m in height is 'high rise' and gets 2016's Annex E treatment (firefighting shaft, refuge-area-adjacent provisions, fire/life-safety audits every 2 years) but would NOT be flagged 'high-rise' at all under 2026's rule. This is one of the most consequential single-number differences between the two editions for any mid-rise (15-24 m) building being evaluated under the wrong edition.
high_rise_definition.not_a_tier_system: Confirmed: like 2026, 2016's high-rise flag is a single boolean threshold, not a synthetic tiered Low/Medium/High-rise CLASSIFICATION system. However 2016 does layer several FURTHER numeric bands on top of the base 15 m flag for specific requirements (e.g. Annex E refuge areas required above 24 m and every 15 m thereafter for buildings without balconies; sprinkler feed redundancy above 60/120 m; intermediate pump/storage above 150-175 m; helipad recommended above 200 m; seismic bracing consideration) - these are graduated design requirements MODULATED by height, not a naming/tier scheme, and they parallel (loosely) 2026's Annex D high-rise stacking logic.

occupancy_wide_height_caps_from_table7_n.note: Table 7's notes impose ABSOLUTE upper height limits on where certain occupancies are permitted at all - a concept not present in 2026's applicability_thresholds.json (2026 has no 'building not permitted above height X' rule of this kind for these occupancy groups; verify this is genuinely absent in 2026 rather than just not digitized). Captured here because they function as a second layer of applicability logic in 2016:

caps.rule: Buildings above 15 m in height are not permitted for occupancies A-1 (lodging/rooming) and A-2 (one/two family dwellings).
Buildings above 30 m in height are not permitted for Group B (Educational), Group C (Institutional), Group D (Assembly) and Group F (Mercantile) occupancies.
Buildings above 18 m in height are not permitted for G-1 and G-2 occupancies.
Buildings above 15 m in height are not permitted for G-3 occupancies.

Buildings above 15 m in height are not permitted for Group H (Storage) and Group J (Hazardous) occupancies. Buildings above 45 m in height are not permitted for multi-level car parking (MLCP) occupancy.

performance_based_design.finding: No equivalent to 2026's Annex M (Performance-Based Design, scoped to heritage buildings) was found anywhere in the 2016 source. 2016's own Annex M is a completely different topic - 'FIRE PROTECTION CONSIDERATIONS FOR VENTING IN INDUSTRIAL BUILDINGS'. Performance-based / alternative-compliance design as a formal annex-level concept appears to be a 2026 addition; 2016 has no PBD escape hatch from its prescriptive Table 7 requirements described anywhere in the extracted text.
